newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: HK's Tsang says studying NZ public sector reform.
newsitem.headline: HK's Tsang says studying NZ public sector reform.

text.p: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Thursday he was interested in New Zealand's example of public sector reform and privatisation.

"The public sector reform which has taken place in this country is probably the most advanced in the world," Tsang told a news conference after meeting New Zealand Finance Minister Bill Birch in Wellington.
He said he was interested in New Zealand's experience in public expenditure control, taxation and its adoption of accrual-based government accounting.
New Zealand has created a leaner and more efficient public sector since the mid-1980s by corporatising or privatising government departments.
Tsang said in reply to a question that the Hong Kong government was not currently considering any sales of state assets in view of the impending transition next year from British to Chinese rule.
However, he said this was "certainly a thing we have to consider". The Hong Kong public sector accounts for about 18 percent of GDP, he said.
